thesis: AvePoint (Nasdaq: AVPT), SaaS data governance, security and migration for Microsoft 365 and other platforms. Q3 2026 10-Q (filed 2026-11-05) read in relevant sections. Q3 revenue 131.1M (+19%, 20% constant currency), SaaS revenue 105.5M (+26%), total ARR 495.1M (+27%, +25% constant currency). 9M revenue 372.8M vs 304.8M (+22%); 9M NI 60.8M includes a 16.8M income tax benefit (pretax 43.9M); 9M OCF 71.6M vs 55.6M. Balance sheet 2026-09-30: cash 410.7M, no debt, deferred revenue 213.6M, equity 436.4M. 9M buybacks 141.3M, shares 215.1M to 210.0M since year end. SBC 26.9M in 9M. Close 16.94 (2026-11-19) x 210.08M = 3.56B = 7.3x TTM revenue, FCF yield 2.7%, P/E about 47x on approximate TTM NI 76.4M, 8.2x book (own arithmetic). Possible market view: a mid-growth security software vendor tied to Microsoft, now priced for growth near 20%. Differing evidence: ARR growth reaccelerating to 27%, net cash, buybacks cutting share count, SBC falling in absolute terms. Insider Form 144 sales were frequent in Sep to Oct 2026 (not examined). Not a recommendation.
counterthesis: Valuation is not low: 7.3x revenue, FCF yield 2.7% before SBC (SBC 26.9M in 9M is about 38% of 9M OCF); GAAP earnings are small and flattered by tax benefits. Buyback of 141M in 9M consumed most cash and funds offset to dilution (diluted shares 223.5M weighted). Reliance on Microsoft ecosystem and AI-governance demand narrative; competition from Microsoft native tools and larger security firms. Frequent insider sale filings. Peers and history not compared.
invalidation: Invalidated by ARR growth falling below about 15%, SaaS net retention weakening, Microsoft bundling that removes the product need, FCF falling while SBC rises, or large insider selling with no offsetting buyback.
